chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Al-Qasim, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan, meaning Musa (peace be upon him), about a man who entrusted a man with some valuable wealth, and the man upon whom is the wealth is a man from the Arabs, powerful enough that he does not give him back anything, and he (the entruster) is not able upon him with anything, and the man who entrusted him is a wicked foreigner. So he did not give him anything. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Say to him, Return it to him, for he had entrusted him with an entrustment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning an entrusted item if the trustee refuses to give it back?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) establishes that the validity of the trust (amanah) rests on the divine authority behind the entrustment rather than the moral character or solvency of the trustee. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that fulfilling one's duty to God takes precedence over worldly reciprocity, ensuring the sanctity of contracts is maintained even when the other party is 'khabith' (wicked) or insolvent. It highlights the concept of 'amanat Allah' as an independent spiritual obligation that transcends social or economic dynamics.
